pairs.subject: proof-carrying-agent-actions
pairs.evidence: crates/table-verify/src/lib.rs:104 The verifier takes the file's own format label as the class of proof it owes: a v1-labelled bundle with no v2 fields passes the format check, every v2 check then reads applies:false and drops out of Report::verified, and the only signature over the relabelled file is the producer's agent key. So a producer can strip the v2 records, relabel and re-sign, and the file still verifies; nothing in the file it cannot re-sign (e.g. the owner-signed decision rows) sets a floor.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-verify/src/lib.rs:104 The version comes from the file's label, not from evidence the producer cannot re-sign. The obvious relabel is refused (line 101, has_v2_fields), but a stripped and re-signed v1 file is read under the lighter rules. authority.rs:152 also relaxes the owner-decision demand for Reader::Verifier on v1. This is exactly the downgrade the technique names.

crates/table-verify/src/main.rs:29 Each check line keeps three states (ok / checked / applies, printed as ✓ ✗ -), but Report::verified is a bool and the CLI exits 1 for both 'failed' and 'could not be checked'. The third value dies at the process boundary, so a not-checked file falls through to fail. Exit 2 covers only unreadable input.

crates/table-verify/src/lib.rs:528 The verifier recomputes the evidence commitment, the checklist hashes (v2.rs:76), the transcript chain and the bindings. It never reads a stated verdict from the file. The format-label issue is recorded under proof-class.

crates/table-verify/src/authority_tests.rs:192 Dishonest bundles go through verify_bundle and must fail with their reason named; one forgery per test. The CLI exit mapping is not exercised in this context.

crates/table-verify/src/main.rs:95 The verdict is printed, not stored for a later merge gate. The Report names the deal and owner key but not a bundle digest or the verifier build; that would matter only if verdicts were stored.
crates/table-verify/src/lib.rs:557 The verifier judges signed deal bundles, not code diffs, so no test file is in its input.

pairs.registryProposal: The format-version downgrade rule fits a non-code domain here: a signed deal-evidence bundle whose producer (the agent key) can re-sign a v1 relabel. That is a good application example. Separately, the technique could say what 'wait' means for an offline, person-run verifier that has no gate: a distinct exit code is the whole remedy.
